shortlist.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Object Detection on Edge Computing Devices
shortlist.abstract: The authors evaluate YOLOv8 (Nano, Small, Medium), EfficientDet Lite variants, and SSD across Raspberry Pi variants and Jetson Orin Nano devices, measuring inference latency, power consumption, and mean Average Precision. They find that lower mAP models such as SSD MobileNet V1 are more energy-efficient and faster, while YOLOv8 Medium demands more resources; TPU accelerators improve performance, and INT8 quantization reduces latency on the Jetson Orin Nano to as low as 23 ms for YOLOv8n.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The single most directly relevant benchmark paper for the project: it directly tests YOLOv8 Nano/Small/Medium on the exact target hardware (Jetson Orin Nano) and reports 23 ms latency with INT8 quantization, validating the team's <50 ms safety loop budget. Provides actionable latency, mAP, and power trade-off data. Weakness is that robustness testing (occlusion, low-light) is absent, and indoor-specific scenarios are not evaluated.

shortlist.title: A Performance Analysis of You Only Look Once Models for Deployment on Constrained Computational Edge Devices in Drone Applications
shortlist.abstract: The paper investigates deploying YOLOv8n and YOLOv8s on Jetson Orin Nano, Orin NX, and Raspberry Pi 5 for drone computer vision, evaluating detection accuracy, inference speed, and energy consumption with post-training quantization. YOLOv8n achieves 52 FPS on Jetson Orin NX and 65 FPS with INT8 quantization via TensorRT. The Raspberry Pi 5 failed to meet real-time requirements. The study identifies latency trade-offs between edge and cloud processing architectures.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Provides peer-reviewed FPS data for YOLOv8n/s on Jetson Orin Nano and Orin NX with TensorRT INT8 optimization, directly applicable to the wheelchair team's hardware. The 52-65 FPS range on Orin NX gives the upper performance envelope while the Orin Nano data sets the floor, both critical for planning pipeline throughput. Energy consumption data is a useful secondary metric for battery-powered wheelchair deployment.

shortlist.title: Autonomous Navigation in Dynamic Human Environments with an Embedded 2D LiDAR-based Person Tracker
shortlist.abstract: This paper presents a real-time tracking system combining a 2D LiDAR-based human detection network and an efficient multi-object tracker, integrated with navigation planning on a quadruped robot. The system achieves 85.45% average MOTA while running at 20 Hz on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX platform, validated in real-world experiments showing how accurate person tracking enhances collision avoidance in shared environments.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Highest-scoring paper: a complete 2D LiDAR person tracker running at 20 Hz on a Jetson Xavier NX in real dynamic indoor environments, directly mirroring the wheelchair's sensor configuration and hardware class. Achieves 85.45% MOTA with validated collision avoidance integration, demonstrating that the LiDAR-side of the perception pipeline is feasible at the required frequency. The coupling to a navigation planner closely parallels the team's Nav2 safety loop architecture.

shortlist.title: Onboard Dynamic-Object Detection and Tracking for Autonomous Robot Navigation with RGB-D Camera
shortlist.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), Vol. 9, No. 1, pp. 651-658
shortlist.abstract: A lightweight detection and tracking system for small robots in crowded environments uses an RGB-D camera with a novel ensemble detection strategy combining multiple computationally efficient but low-accuracy detectors to achieve real-time high-accuracy obstacle detection. The system achieves 0.11 m position error and 0.23 m/s velocity error when tested on a quadcopter's onboard computer, and is released as an open-source ROS package.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Published in RA-L (strong venue) and validated on real embedded hardware running ROS with an RGB-D camera in crowded environments. The 0.11 m position accuracy at real-time rates on a resource-constrained onboard computer is directly transferable to the wheelchair's RealSense + Jetson setup. Open-source ROS package lowers integration effort. Crowded-environment testing provides partial robustness evidence.

shortlist.title: A Real-Time Dynamic Obstacle Tracking and Mapping System for UAV Navigation and Collision Avoidance with an RGB-D Camera
shortlist.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2023
shortlist.abstract: A real-time system for UAVs equipped with RGB-D cameras (Intel RealSense D435i) to perceive and avoid obstacles in crowded environments combines occupancy voxel mapping for identifying dynamic obstacles, Kalman and continuity filters for tracking, and Markov chain-based trajectory prediction. It distinguishes stationary from moving obstacles and is computationally efficient for resource-constrained UAVs, released as an open-source ROS package.
shortlist.evaluator_note: ICRA 2023 paper using exactly the same sensor (Intel RealSense D435i) as the wheelchair project, demonstrating real-time dynamic obstacle detection+tracking+mapping on resource-constrained embedded hardware in crowded environments. The static/dynamic obstacle separation approach is critical for maintaining a clean Nav2 costmap. Open-source ROS package directly reusable by the team.

shortlist.title: ByteTrack: Multi-Object Tracking by Associating Every Detection Box
shortlist.abstract: ByteTrack associates every detection box (including low-confidence ones) with existing tracklets, rather than discarding low-score detections. By leveraging similarities between low-confidence detections and tracklets to recover true objects and filter background, it achieves 80.3 MOTA, 77.3 IDF1, and 63.1 HOTA on MOT17 at 30 FPS on a V100 GPU. It yields consistent improvement across 9 state-of-the-art trackers.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The dominant default tracker paired with YOLO in virtually all modern real-time pedestrian tracking deployments, including Ultralytics YOLOv8's built-in tracker. Its low-confidence detection association is critical for tracking partially occluded pedestrians near a wheelchair. ECCV 2022 publication with strong empirical benchmarks on MOT17/20. Marked seminal as it is the de facto baseline for any YOLO+tracking pipeline.

shortlist.title: Observation-Centric SORT: Rethinking SORT for Robust Multi-Object Tracking
shortlist.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2023
shortlist.abstract: OC-SORT addresses limitations of Kalman filter-based MOT during occlusions and non-linear motion by using an observation-centric approach. Instead of linear state predictions, it computes a virtual trajectory over occlusion periods from detector measurements to fix error accumulation. OC-SORT achieves real-time performance at 700+ FPS on a single CPU and sets state-of-the-art on MOT17, MOT20, KITTI, and DanceTrack.
shortlist.evaluator_note: 700+ FPS on CPU makes OC-SORT the most efficient tracker in the candidate pool, leaving GPU budget free for YOLO inference on the Jetson. Its explicit occlusion correction via virtual trajectories addresses a core failure mode in indoor wheelchair navigation (people stepping behind furniture). CVPR 2023 publication with rigorous multi-benchmark evaluation including non-linear motion datasets.

shortlist.title: HopTrack: A Real-time Multi-Object Tracking System for Embedded Devices
shortlist.abstract: HopTrack is a real-time multi-object tracking system designed for embedded devices, using a novel discretized static and dynamic matching approach and a content-aware dynamic sampling technique. On Jetson AGX Xavier, it achieves 39.29 FPS with 63.12% MOTA on MOT16, while reducing energy consumption by 20.8%, power draw by 5%, and memory usage by 8%. The framework is detector-agnostic.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The only tracker candidate in the pool designed and validated specifically for Jetson-class embedded hardware, achieving 39 FPS on AGX Xavier with MOT16 benchmarks. Energy and memory reductions are important for the wheelchair's battery budget and Orin Nano's 8 GB memory ceiling. Unique in its niche as the embedded-optimized tracker option; included as sole coverage of this design space even though venue is currently preprint.

shortlist.title: A Comprehensive Review of YOLO Architectures in Computer Vision: From YOLOv1 to YOLOv8 and YOLO-NAS
shortlist.venue: Machine Learning and Knowledge Extraction (MDPI), Vol. 5, No. 4
shortlist.abstract: This paper traces the evolution of YOLO across all major versions up to YOLOv8 and YOLO-NAS, covering architectural changes, training methodologies, standard evaluation metrics, and postprocessing approaches. It synthesizes key developmental insights and proposes future research directions for advancing real-time detection capabilities across robotics, autonomous vehicles, and surveillance applications.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The canonical reference for the YOLO family through YOLOv8 and YOLO-NAS. Published in a peer-reviewed MDPI journal with 36 pages of architectural synthesis, this is the standard citation when justifying YOLO selection and comparing variants. Included as seminal: any paper choosing between YOLOv8/v9/v10/YOLO-NAS needs this as its definitional reference. Does not provide edge benchmark numbers itself, which limits direct engineering usefulness.

shortlist.title: YOLOv10: Real-Time End-to-End Object Detection
shortlist.abstract: YOLOv10 eliminates reliance on non-maximum suppression (NMS) post-processing using consistent dual assignments for NMS-free training, and introduces an efficiency-accuracy driven model design strategy. YOLOv10-S is 1.8x faster than RT-DETR-R18 under similar AP on COCO, and YOLOv10-B achieves 46% less latency and 25% fewer parameters than YOLOv9-C at equivalent performance.
shortlist.evaluator_note: NeurIPS 2024 publication with strong empirical benchmarks. The NMS-free design is directly relevant to latency: eliminating NMS post-processing reduces end-to-end latency on the Jetson Orin Nano, which is the binding constraint. The 46% latency reduction over YOLOv9 at equivalent accuracy makes this a strong candidate to replace YOLOv8 as the detection backbone, depending on Jetson TensorRT support.

shortlist.title: DR-SPAAM: A Spatial-Attention and Auto-regressive Model for Person Detection in 2D Range Data
shortlist.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) 2020
shortlist.abstract: DR-SPAAM proposes a forward-looking paradigm for person detection in 2D LiDAR range data, keeping intermediate features from the backbone as a template and recurrently updating it as new scans arrive, avoiding expensive multi-scan alignment. It achieves state-of-the-art results on the DROW dataset at 87.2 FPS on a laptop GPU and 22.6 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX embedded GPU, with a PyTorch implementation and pre-trained models released.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The leading algorithm for 2D LiDAR person detection with confirmed 22.6 FPS on a Jetson AGX embedded GPU — directly applicable to the wheelchair's LiDAR person detection layer. IROS 2020 publication with state-of-the-art results on DROW benchmark. PyTorch + pre-trained models available, providing a plug-in implementation for the team's pipeline. Unique in being the only candidate specifically addressing 2D LiDAR person detection efficiency on embedded GPU.

shortlist.title: JRDB: A Dataset and Benchmark of Egocentric Robot Visual Perception of Humans in Built Environments
shortlist.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI)
shortlist.abstract: JRDB is an egocentric dataset collected from JackRabbot, a social mobile manipulator, comprising 64 minutes of annotated multimodal sensor data including 360° stereo RGB video, 3D point clouds from multiple lidar systems, audio, RGB-D footage, and fisheye imagery. It features 2.3 million bounding boxes and 1.8 million 3D cuboids across over 3,500 human trajectories in indoor and outdoor environments, with benchmarks and metrics for person detection and tracking.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The definitive benchmark dataset for egocentric robot-viewpoint person detection and tracking in indoor environments, published in TPAMI (highest-tier CV venue). The low sensor height, indoor scenes with crowding, and multimodal sensor suite (LiDAR + RGB-D) mirror the wheelchair's configuration. Essential for evaluating any detection/tracking model trained or tested from a robot's perspective. Marked seminal for its unique coverage of this evaluation niche.

shortlist.title: A Comparative Study of 3D Person Detection: Sensor Modalities and Robustness in Diverse Indoor and Outdoor Environments
shortlist.venue: International Conference on Computer Vision Theory and Applications (VISAPP) 2026
shortlist.abstract: This study evaluates camera-only (BEVDepth), LiDAR-only (PointPillars), and fusion-based (DAL) 3D person detection approaches using the JRDB dataset across varying occlusion and distance levels in indoor and outdoor scenes. Fusion models provide superior results in challenging conditions, though DAL remains sensitive to sensor misalignment and LiDAR-based corruptions. The camera-based approach showed weakest performance under occlusion.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Provides the only direct empirical comparison of camera-only vs LiDAR-only vs fusion for 3D person detection on JRDB, the most relevant robot-viewpoint benchmark. The finding that camera-only fails worst under occlusion and that fusion outperforms single modalities directly justifies the team's RGB-D + LiDAR fusion architecture choice. Recency (2026) ensures coverage of current SOTA. Weakness is lack of real-time or edge deployment metrics.

shortlist.title: Efficient Obstacle Detection and Tracking Using RGB-D Sensor Data in Dynamic Environments for Robotic Applications
shortlist.abstract: This paper employs a u-depth map for obstacle detection with dynamic thresholding on depth images, introduces a restricted v-depth map technique for improved dimension estimation, and presents a new algorithm to track obstacles until they leave the field of view. Testing across multiple datasets shows the method outperforms vision-based state-of-the-art methods in state estimation of dynamic obstacles and execution time.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Validated on Intel RealSense D435i (the same sensor as the wheelchair project) at 60 Hz on Jetson TX2 with 0.6 ms per detection — far below the 50 ms budget. Provides a lightweight, non-learning baseline for depth-image-based detection+tracking that can run as a safety fallback when the YOLO model is overloaded. Dynamic thresholding on depth images is a practical approach for handling highly varied indoor obstacle heights.

shortlist.title: From the Desks of ROS Maintainers: A Survey of Modern & Capable Mobile Robotics Algorithms in the Robot Operating System 2
shortlist.abstract: Written by key ROS Navigation maintainers, this survey examines the state of robotic navigation in ROS 2, covering new systems without parallel in ROS 1 and discussing both contemporary research and established methods across various robot types. It covers Nav2 planners (Hybrid A*, Smac, MPPI), costmap layers, SLAM integration, and addresses dynamic environments, along with implementations not yet documented in academic literature.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Written by the actual Nav2 maintainers, this is the authoritative reference for the ROS2/Nav2 stack that will serve as the wheelchair's fast safety loop. Covers costmap design, dynamic obstacle layers, MPPI local planner, and SLAM integration — all components the perception pipeline must feed into. Included as seminal: essential for any team implementing Nav2-based shared autonomy.

shortlist.title: From Detection to Action Recognition: An Edge-Based Pipeline for Robot Human Perception
shortlist.abstract: A complete processing pipeline for mobile service robots integrates human detection, tracking, and action recognition, operating in near real-time while ensuring all stages run on the edge to minimize dependence on centralized servers. Various state-of-the-art models were tested for performance and efficiency, and evaluated on a custom household activity dataset, demonstrating applicability in healthcare and assisted living environments.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The closest architectural analogue to the project: a complete edge-deployed human detection+tracking pipeline on a mobile service robot in healthcare/assisted living settings, running without cloud infrastructure. Directly informs pipeline architecture choices. Healthcare/assisted living domain matches the wheelchair's operational context better than any other candidate. Weakness is that it is a preprint without specific hardware names or quantitative latency numbers in the abstract.

shortlist.title: Panopticus: Omnidirectional 3D Object Detection on Resource-constrained Edge Devices
shortlist.venue: ACM International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking (MobiCom) 2024
shortlist.abstract: Panopticus uses an adaptive multi-branch detection scheme that dynamically adjusts model architecture based on available hardware resources and spatial complexities for 360-degree 3D detection on edge devices. It improves accuracy by 62% on average given a strict 33 ms latency objective, and achieves 2.1x latency reduction compared to baselines. For Jetson Orin Nano (6.3 GB memory), large modules are detached to prevent memory overloading.
shortlist.evaluator_note: MobiCom 2024 (top systems venue) paper that explicitly addresses the 33 ms latency constraint on Jetson Orin Nano by name, providing an adaptive detection architecture that prevents memory overloading on the 6.3 GB device. The adaptive multi-branch scheme — reducing complexity dynamically under resource pressure — is directly applicable when the wheelchair runs YOLO+tracker+LiDAR+SLAM concurrently. Provides the strongest evidence that 3D detection under strict latency is achievable on Orin Nano.

shortlist.title: Benchmarking Jetson Edge Devices with an End-to-End Video-Based Anomaly Detection System
shortlist.venue: Future of Information and Communication Conference (FICC) 2024
shortlist.abstract: Researchers deployed a video-based anomaly detection system across NVIDIA Jetson Nano, AGX Xavier, and Orin Nano, achieving 47.56 FPS inference speed on a Jetson edge device with only 3.11 GB RAM usage using TorchTensorRT optimization. The Jetson Orin Nano delivers 15% better performance than its predecessor while consuming 50% less energy.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Provides concrete Jetson Orin Nano throughput (47.56 FPS, 3.11 GB RAM) and energy comparisons for an end-to-end video pipeline — useful for estimating overall system headroom on the wheelchair's Orin Nano. The 15% performance gain and 50% energy reduction over prior Jetson generation quantifies the hardware improvement directly. Included as unique coverage of multi-generational Jetson benchmarking with TensorRT, relevant to hardware procurement decisions.

shortlist.title: Real-time Monocular Depth Estimation on Embedded Systems
shortlist.venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP) 2024
shortlist.abstract: The paper proposes RT-MonoDepth and RT-MonoDepth-S, two lightweight neural network models for monocular depth estimation balancing computational efficiency with accuracy. On Jetson Nano, the models achieve 18–31 FPS; on Jetson AGX Orin, 253–364 FPS at 640x192 resolution. They deliver accuracy comparable to prior depth estimation methods while executing substantially faster than existing lightweight alternatives on the KITTI dataset.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Provides 364 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin and 31 FPS on Jetson Nano for monocular depth estimation — confirming that a monocular depth fallback for the RealSense is computationally viable on the Orin Nano at very low cost. ICIP 2024 publication with rigorous latency benchmarks across multiple Jetson generations. Unique in its niche as the only candidate reporting monocular depth FPS on Jetson hardware.

excluded.reason: YOLOv9 is a useful YOLO variant but does not report latency or edge deployment benchmarks in the paper itself; YOLOv10 (NeurIPS 2024) supersedes it on both efficiency and rigor. Total score estimated at 13/25 (rigor:4, relevance:3, latency:2, robustness:2, edge:2).

RT-DETR is a strong detector but benchmarks are on T4 GPU (server-class hardware), not edge devices. Transformer encoder is likely too slow for Jetson Orin Nano within the 50 ms budget without significant quantization work not yet demonstrated. Total score estimated at 14/25 (rigor:5, relevance:3, latency:4, robustness:2, edge:2) — borderline, excluded in favor of keeping shortlist focused on validated edge-deployable detectors.

StrongSORT is a strong multi-object tracker but adds significant computational overhead vs ByteTrack/OC-SORT due to re-identification features. The team's indoor environment with intermittent re-identification needs is better served by ByteTrack (speed) or OC-SORT (occlusion). Total score estimated at 14/25 (rigor:4, relevance:3, latency:3, robustness:3, edge:2) — borderline but excluded to maintain shortlist at 18 or fewer.

BoT-SORT's camera-motion compensation is useful for a mobile platform, but the paper is an arXiv preprint without confirmed peer review and its ReID variant adds latency inappropriate for a resource-constrained Jetson. OC-SORT and ByteTrack better cover this tracking niche with superior rigor. Total score estimated at 13/25 (rigor:2, relevance:3, latency:3, robustness:3, edge:2).

DeepSORT (2017) is historically important but substantially superseded by ByteTrack, OC-SORT, StrongSORT, and BoT-SORT. Its deep ReID features are too slow for real-time Jetson Orin Nano deployment. ByteTrack is already marked seminal for the tracking niche. Total score estimated at 12/25 (rigor:3, relevance:3, latency:2, robustness:3, edge:2).

DROW (2016) is the foundational 2D LiDAR person detection dataset and approach, but DR-SPAAM (2020) supersedes it methodologically and achieves better performance on the same DROW benchmark. Functionally redundant with DR-SPAAM in the shortlist. Total score estimated at 13/25 (rigor:4, relevance:4, latency:2, robustness:2, edge:2).

Depth Anything V1 is superseded by V2 in the same year; V2 offers strictly better accuracy and efficiency at all model sizes. No edge/Jetson benchmarks reported in either paper, limiting direct engineering utility. Excluded in favor of V2 and RT-MonoDepth which provides actual Jetson FPS numbers. Total score estimated at 12/25 (rigor:4, relevance:3, latency:2, robustness:2, edge:1).

Depth Anything V2 is a strong monocular depth foundation model but reports no Jetson or edge deployment benchmarks, making it hard to assess runtime feasibility. RT-MonoDepth (ICIP 2024) fills the same niche with confirmed Jetson FPS numbers. DA-V2 could serve as a fine-tuned backbone but its deployment feasibility on Orin Nano is unverified. Total score estimated at 13/25 (rigor:4, relevance:3, latency:2, robustness:2, edge:2).

BEVFusion-based semantic occupancy grids are computationally intensive and designed for autonomous vehicle hardware budgets. No real-time runtime metrics are reported in the paper. The approach is conceptually relevant but not validated on Jetson-class hardware. Total score estimated at 12/25 (rigor:4, relevance:3, latency:1, robustness:3, edge:1).

Proposes an interesting dynamic object removal approach for SLAM but is an arXiv preprint with no quantitative accuracy improvements reported in the abstract and no hardware runtime validation. Weaker rigor than Long et al. 2023 which covers the same SLAM+dynamics niche with more detail. Total score estimated at 10/25 (rigor:2, relevance:3, latency:2, robustness:2, edge:1).

Addresses a real need (SLAM under heavy occlusion in dynamic indoor environments) but is an arXiv preprint with only qualitative performance claims. No quantitative localization error metrics or timing data reported. Relevant but insufficient rigor evidence to include over the threshold. Total score estimated at 13/25 (rigor:2, relevance:4, latency:2, robustness:3, edge:2).

Pedestrian trajectory prediction is in scope for the slow LLM loop (handled by teammates) rather than the fast perception pipeline. The paper is an arXiv preprint with no real-robot or edge hardware validation. Marginal relevance to the team's specific non-LLM perception pipeline task. Total score estimated at 11/25 (rigor:2, relevance:2, latency:2, robustness:3, edge:1).

Demonstrates trajectory prediction + motion planning on a real indoor service robot with RGB-D, which is relevant, but the paper focuses on the planning layer rather than the perception pipeline. GPU-accelerated planning is not directly applicable to Jetson Orin Nano within the team's architecture. Total score estimated at 13/25 (rigor:4, relevance:3, latency:3, robustness:2, edge:2).

YOLO-IHD achieves 27 FPS on Jetson Nano (validated hardware) for indoor human detection, which is a relevant result. However, the drone overhead viewpoint is significantly different from the wheelchair's lateral viewpoint, and the IHD dataset domain is not directly transferable. Borderline at estimated 14/25 (rigor:3, relevance:3, latency:4, robustness:3, edge:4) — excluded because the shortlist already has stronger YOLO+edge candidates and this provides minimal unique coverage not addressed by alqahtani_2024 or rey_2025.

metadata.note: Target threshold of 14/25 applied as specified. Several papers included below 18/25 where they are the unique or best coverage of a technique critical to the pipeline (e.g., HopTrack for embedded MOT, RT-MonoDepth for Jetson depth estimation, DROW/DR-SPAAM for 2D LiDAR detection). The threshold was not lowered; 18 papers made the shortlist, within the 12–18 target range.
